responseText:
Short answer (one line)
- A “searchable” PDF contains real text data you can search/select/copy; a “scanned” PDF is just images of pages (no real text) unless OCR was added.

Quick explanation to use at lunch
- Scanned PDF: each page is a picture (an image XObject). You can view and print it, but you can’t highlight, copy text, or use Find because there’s no text inside—just pixels.
- Searchable PDF (born-digital): the file contains real text objects (characters, font info, and positioning). You can search, select, copy/paste, and screen readers can read it.
- Scanned + OCR (common hybrid): you scanned pages to images, then ran OCR. The PDF still has the page images, but it also includes an invisible text layer (the OCR output) aligned with the image. That makes it “searchable” even though the original content came from a scan.

A bit more technical (if your coworker asks)
- PDFs store content in content streams. Text is encoded using PDF text operators (Tj, TJ, etc.) with font resources and (ideally) a ToUnicode mapping so characters map to Unicode for copying/searching.
- Scans are stored as image XObjects placed on the page; no text operators are present.
- OCR adds text either as visible text objects with transparent rendering or as a separate hidden layer/annotation so the text is indexable and selectable while the image remains visible.
- A properly “born-digital” PDF usually has clean text and tagging (structure tree, ToUnicode maps), making it accessible and reliable for extraction. OCRed text can have recognition errors, wrong word breaks, or bad encodings.

How you can tell quickly
- Try selecting text or using Ctrl/Cmd+F to find a word. If it works, it’s searchable. If selection only highlights the whole page or nothing, it’s image-only.
- In Acrobat Reader: Tools → Accessibility or View → Show/Hide → Navigation Panes → Content to inspect objects. In command-line tools: pdffonts shows embedded fonts; pdfgrep or strings can hint at embedded text.
- File size: image-only PDFs tend to be larger per page; not a definitive test but a clue.

Why it matters
- Searchability/indexing (find, grep, document management systems)
- Copy/paste and accurate text extraction
- Accessibility (screen readers need real text and tags)
- Reliability: OCRed text may be imperfect; born-digital text is usually accurate.

One-liner you can send your coworker
- “Scanned = page images only; searchable = contains actual text objects (or an OCR text layer) so you can find and copy text.”
